recommended_purchase.author: F. Alton Everest

recommended_purchase.author: Floyd Toole

recommended_purchase.title: Music by the Numbers: From Pythagoras to Schoenberg
recommended_purchase.author: Eli Maor
recommended_purchase.notes: Accessible narrative history of music-math connections. Princeton UP, 176 pages.

recommended_purchase.title: The Physics of Music: The Science of Musical Sound
recommended_purchase.author: Various (Dover reprint)
recommended_purchase.notes: Dover Publications reprint — affordable classic on musical acoustics.

recommended_purchase.title: Every Brain Needs Music: The Neuroscience of Making and Listening to Music
recommended_purchase.author: Lawrence Sherman & Dennis Plies
recommended_purchase.notes: Columbia UP, 2023. Covers the neurological basis of music perception.

recommended_purchase.title: Music, Math, and Mind: The Physics and Neuroscience of Music
recommended_purchase.author: David Sulzer (aka Dave Soldier)
recommended_purchase.notes: Columbia UP, 2021. Dual-perspective from a Columbia neuroscience professor and experimental musician. Covers math of scales, tuning, psychoacoustics, and animal sound.

recommended_purchase.title: Mathemagical Music Production
recommended_purchase.author: Derrick Scott van Heerden
recommended_purchase.notes: Self-published, 2016. Applies ancient mathematical principles to modern production. 432 Hz perspective — useful for Robert Edward Grant-adjacent research.

recommended_purchase.title: From Music to Mathematics: Exploring the Connections
recommended_purchase.author: Gareth E. Roberts
recommended_purchase.notes: Johns Hopkins UP. 'Music first' approach — musical examples motivate mathematical depth. Highly regarded textbook.

recommended_purchase.title: Music and Mathematics: From Pythagoras to Fractals
recommended_purchase.author: John Fauvel, Raymond Flood & Robin Wilson (eds.)
recommended_purchase.notes: Oxford UP. Multi-author collection by leading scholars. Covers physical, theoretical, physiological, and compositional connections.

recommended_purchase.title: Mathematical Music Theory: Algebraic, Geometric, Combinatorial, Topological and Applied Approaches
recommended_purchase.author: Mariana Montiel & Robert W. Peck (eds.)
recommended_purchase.notes: World Scientific, 2018. Advanced academic treatment. Includes chapters by Dmitri Tymoczko and Jason Yust on geometric Tonnetz generalizations.

recommended_purchase.title: The Geometry of Musical Rhythm: What Makes a 'Good' Rhythm Good?
recommended_purchase.author: Godfried T. Toussaint
recommended_purchase.notes: CRC Press. Widely cited. Explores rhythm mathematically through geometric lenses — Euclidean algorithms, necklaces, and polygonal representations.

recommended_purchase.title: Microtonality and the Tuning Systems of Erv Wilson
recommended_purchase.author: Terumi Narushima
recommended_purchase.notes: Routledge Studies in Music Theory. First book-length treatment of Wilson's theories. Essential for xenharmonic geometry work.

recommended_purchase.title: Tuning and Temperament: A Historical Survey
recommended_purchase.author: J. Murray Barbour
recommended_purchase.notes: Dover reprint. Classic 1932 scholarly survey of Western tuning history. Foundational xenharmonic reference.

recommended_purchase.title: The Structure of Recognizable Diatonic Tunings
recommended_purchase.author: Easley Blackwood
recommended_purchase.notes: Princeton UP, 1985. Theoretical analysis of EDO systems from 12 to 24 tones. Key reference in xenharmonic theory.

recommended_purchase.title: Genesis of a Music
recommended_purchase.author: Harry Partch
recommended_purchase.notes: Da Capo Press. The foundational text of 20th-century microtonal composition. Combines theory, aesthetics, and instrument design.

recommended_purchase.title: How Equal Temperament Ruined Harmony (and Why You Should Care)
recommended_purchase.author: Ross W. Duffin
recommended_purchase.notes: W.W. Norton, 2007. Accessible argument for historical temperaments. Good entry point for non-specialists.

recommended_purchase.title: Mathematical Theory of Music
recommended_purchase.author: Franck Jedrzejewski
recommended_purchase.notes: Delatour France / IRCAM, 2006. Advanced mathematical treatment of music theory. Referenced on the Xenharmonic Wiki.

recommended_purchase.title: The Math Behind the Music
recommended_purchase.author: Leon Harkleroad
recommended_purchase.notes: Cambridge UP / MAA Outlooks series. Concise, accessible overview of mathematics in music for general audiences.

recommended_purchase.title: Tuning In: Microtonality, Temperaments and Artful Microtuning for Synthesizers
recommended_purchase.author: Scott Wilkinson & Wendy Carlos
recommended_purchase.notes: Hal Leonard, 1988. Practical guide to microtuning synthesizers. Historically significant, co-authored by Wendy Carlos.

journals.name: Music Theory Spectrum
journals.publisher: Oxford University Press / Society for Music Theory
journals.notes: Premier peer-reviewed journal of the Society for Music Theory. Offers separate RSS feeds for latest issue, advance articles, and open-access articles.

journals.name: Journal of New Music Research
journals.notes: Founded 1972 as Interface. Broad scope: popular music, world music, classical. Quantitative and empirical methods. Vol 54 (2025) current.

journals.name: Psychomusicology: Music, Mind, and Brain
journals.notes: APA journal covering cognitive and neuroscientific aspects of music. Companion to Music Perception.

journals.name: Auditory Perception & Cognition
journals.notes: Covers localization, motion perception, auditory scene analysis, pitch, loudness, timbre, music and speech perception.

journals.name: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America (JASA)

rss_feeds.name: Sevish — Microtonal / Xenharmonic Blog
rss_feeds.notes: The most actively updated xenharmonic blog. Sevish is also creator of Scale Workshop. Posts through Feb 2026.

rss_feeds.name: PostClassic — Kyle Gann (ArtsJournal)
rss_feeds.notes: Kyle Gann is one of the foremost writers on just intonation and microtonality. His kylegann.com site also has comprehensive tuning theory reference pages.

rss_feeds.name: Now and Xen Podcast
rss_feeds.notes: The primary podcast dedicated to xenharmonic music. Long-form interviews with microtonal composers and theorists. Active since 2018. ~83 min avg episode.

rss_feeds.name: SMT-Pod (Society for Music Theory Podcast)
rss_feeds.notes: Academic podcast from the Society for Music Theory. Season 4 (Spring 2025) underway. Scholarly level.

rss_feeds.name: Journal of Mathematics and Music — RSS
Journal of New Music Research — RSS
arXiv — math.HO (History and Overview, includes music theory)
arXiv — math.CO (Combinatorics, includes pitch-class & rhythm geometry)

websites.name: Kyle Gann — Just Intonation Explained
websites.notes: The definitive accessible introduction to just intonation. Essential reading. Also check kylegann.com/microtonality.html for extended theory.

websites.name: Sound American — Just Intonation Issue
websites.notes: Deep-dive editorial collection on just intonation in contemporary composition.

websites.name: CymaScope
websites.notes: John Stuart Reid's patented instrument making sound visible. Research includes work in the King's Chamber of the Great Pyramid. Quantum physics connections. Already a YouTube source in Convex.

websites.name: Harmonics of Nature
websites.notes: Explores connections between harmonics, geometry, and nature. Active through 2025.

websites.name: Huygens-Fokker Foundation
websites.notes: Primary home of the Scala tuning software. Comprehensive library of scales, tuning theory, and the Fokker periodicity block system. Essential for microtuning work.

websites.name: Xenharmonic Wiki
websites.notes: Community-maintained encyclopedia of xenharmonic music theory. The Library page (en.xen.wiki/w/The_Library) has the best curated bibliography in the field.

websites.name: Xenharmonic Wiki — Microtonal Blogs
websites.notes: Curated list of active and archived microtonal blogs with links. Use this to find more RSS sources.

websites.name: Huygens-Fokker Scala Scale Archive
websites.notes: Archive of thousands of Scala (.scl) tuning files. Directly relevant to the scales/ directory in this project.

websites.name: Sevish — Scale Workshop (web app)
websites.notes: Browser-based tool for creating and exploring microtonal scales. Exports Scala files compatible with this project.

websites.name: Cosmic Core — Sound, Waves & Cymatics Articles
websites.notes: Deep exploration of how vibrations create geometry. Aligns with Robert Edward Grant's polygon-angle research.

arxiv_categories.name: History and Overview (includes mathematical music theory)
arxiv_categories.notes: Best arXiv category for music-math papers: Tonnetz, tuning theory, group theory applications to music.
